correctness.rationale: A Boolean congruence is determined by the atoms in its kernel ideal, and f respects it iff those atoms are forward closed: necessity uses a witnessing single-atom toggle, and sufficiency factors any equivalent pair into such toggles. On an invariant partition algebra the analogous statement uses whole blocks and the induced dependency graph. Restriction of a global kernel collapses exactly the blocks wholly contained in it, so the least globally compatible kernel containing the local blocks extends the local congruence iff reachability has not swallowed an outside block. All Boolean subalgebras arise from partitions; no monotonicity is needed. For the census I generated scalar tables by enumerating antichains of minimal true inputs (20) and tested actual congruence relations by related pairs and exact restriction, with no graph criterion or frozen source code. The complete labelled counts reproduced 8000, 5249/2751 pass/fail, 4273/2586 normal pass/fail, 4520 nonadditive passes and 729 additive passes. Canonical conjugates gave 1440/492 total/failing orbits; fixed totals/failures were 8000/2751, 200/65 and 20/3 for identity, transpositions and 3-cycles. The auxiliary normal closure totals were 32/13 pass/fail.
residual_risks: Exhaustiveness of the counts is specific to three atoms. The all-finite criterion is proved separately by the kernel argument; no statement about generated varieties follows.

value.rationale: Isotonicity and normality are intrinsic operator hypotheses in the CEP literature, not artificial filters. The first carrier on which failure is possible gives an interpretable cutoff, and count and orbit frequencies distinguish the consequences of these hypotheses without conflating algebras and varieties. The minimal-kernel reachability criterion also provides an explicit obstruction and an explicit extension when one exists.
residual_risks: No enumeration is claimed for larger carriers, and the partition criterion is not claimed to be efficient there.
